en: The Eightfold Hymn of the Names of Śiva:
O Moon-crested One, Destroyer of Madana, Trident-bearer,
Sthāṇu, Lord of the Mountains, Lord of Girijā, Maheśa, Śambhu!

O Lord of the World, O beloved of Pārvatī’s heart, O moon-crested one, protect the world— its protector and the destroyer of the fear of those afraid of Bhūteśa— from the dense thicket of the suffering of saṃsāra.
O Lord of beings, O Pramathanātha, O Girīśa, O wielder of the bow;
O Vāmadeva, O Bhava, O Rudra, O Pinākapāṇi, [save me] from saṃsāra...
O Nīlakaṇṭha, O Vṛṣabhadhvaja, O Pañcavaktra!
O Lord of the World, O Śeṣavalaya, O Lord of the Pramathas, O Śarva!
O Dhūrjaṭi, O Paśupati, O Lord of Girijā, [save] me from saṃsāra...
O Viśvanātha, O Śiva, O Śaṅkara, O God of gods!
O Gaṅgādhara, O Leader of the Pramathas, O Nandikeśa; O Bāṇeśvara, O Enemy of Andhaka, O Hara, O Lord of the World, O [Lord of] Saṃsāra... ||4|| O Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, O Maṇikarṇikeśa!
O Vīreśa, O Lord of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, O All-pervading One, O Gaṇeśa!
O Omniscient One, sole abode within the hearts of all, [refuge] from the cycle of existence...
5 O glorious Maheśvara, full of grace, O Compassionate One!
O Vyomakeśa, Śitikaṇṭha, Lord of the Gaṇas;
O you whose limbs are smeared with ashes, who wear a garland of a collection of human skulls; O you who dwell on Mount Kailāsa, O Vṛṣākapi! [Save me from] the cycle of existence... 6.
O Conqueror of Death, three-eyed one, abode of the three worlds!
O Lord of Śakti, who removes the pride of Nārāyaṇa, [liberator from] saṃsāra...
O Lord of the Universe, destroyer of the world's existence, you whose form is the universe!
O Soul of the Universe, Sole Lord of the three worlds preeminent in virtues;
O Viśvanātha, embodiment of compassion, Friend of the wretched!
To Maheśvara, the abode of Gaurī’s delights... 8... [Salutation].
Salutations to that Śiva, the five-faced one who provides refuge, the destroyer of all, the sovereign lord of the entire world, and the burner away of the suffering of poverty. 9.

Thus ends the *Śivanāmāvalyaṣṭaka*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (*paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya*).
